name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Full lifecycle: greenfield genesis (architect → explore → design) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → optional /spec:design (mock-bound, deterministic fidelity gates) → /spec:build (direct Sonnet worker dispatch per layer wave, executed red-check) → /spec:review (deterministic legs via review-legs.js + ONE fresh-context reviewer whose non-soft findings carry executed repros; verdict derived by verdict.js) → /spec:release, plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.11.0 — fleet evidence reader: a new zero-dependency script (`spec/scripts/fleet-reader.js`, `spec-paths fleet-reader`) scans every repo one level under `~/Projects` carrying `.claude/spec.config.json`, reads each in-scope repo's `.claude/spec-runs*.jsonl` ledgers (live plus year archives), and answers six fixed queries — leg red-recency, the brief-08 gate, escape aggregates, replay debt, CLEAN-contradicted-by-escape, and a schema-drift census — population-first (repos scanned, rows read, unparseable counts, oldest/newest ts always lead both renders, and a config-bearing repo with no ledger still lists at rows: 0), read-only and stateless (no writes, no cache, no stored repo list), `--json` (seven top-level keys) or a human render. Brief 17's motivating gap: pipeline questions were being answered from this repo's own ledger, ~14% of the 1,077 rows readable fleet-wide today. Two JJ-ruled doctrine changes ride along: core.md § Incident Policy's third-recurrence trigger now counts across every readable repo ledger on this machine (26 fleet-wide escapes vs at most 13 visible in any one repo) rather than one host's slice, deriving from the literal invocation `node "$(spec-paths fleet-reader)" --json`; and `/spec:escape`'s row schema gains a nullable `class` field (a stable kebab-case defect-class id, derived from evidence and confirmed in the existing classification call, `null` when underivable) so defect-class recurrence — the trigger's numerator — becomes mechanically countable going forward instead of forever hand-asserted. The reader is deliberately boring: six fixed queries, no query flags, nothing that grows toward the autopilot shape the brief names as its own failure mode. 7.10.0 — admission bar hardened to derivation over attestation (same-day amendment of 7.9.0, backed by a May-2026+ research sweep): the five tests are now five separately answered fields, derived from ledger evidence wherever a ledger can answer them — generality names ≥2 ledger-recorded class members (≥1 not the triggering incident), materiality is the cited fleet recurrence count, removability is a kill condition a ledger query answers with a count, falsifiability cites its executed red run — with portability deliberately left as prose because a synthetic second-stack run is fixture evidence and fixture-fed proof is not terminal; a proposal that cannot fill all five fields is a rejection whose reopen condition must itself be ledger-answerable. Rationale: holistic one-line self-certification is the most inflatable shape (halo effect, up to ~50% inflation in cited studies) while computed numbers cannot be talked into existence. Roadmap brief 17 (fleet evidence reader) is named the bar's evidence source and gains its invocation point — it runs whenever a guard is proposed or a rejection's reopen condition is evaluated — and its escape-aggregate query now flags recurrent-unguarded classes (≥3 recurrences, no standing guard), pricing the bar's rejection bias. Doctrine + roadmap prose only — no script, no schema, no host contract change. 7.9.0 — admission bar for standing guards: core.md § Incident Policy now requires that a guard earned by third recurrence also pass five admission tests — portable across host stacks, general to the class rather than the triggering instance, material (value exceeds maintenance + reading cost), falsified once (deliberately tripped to prove it can go red), and shipped with the kill condition that would retire it — and a proposal that cannot state all five in one line becomes a rejection with a reopen condition; this writes down the missing half of the policy (it said when a guard is earned, never what shape an admitted guard must have), generalizing the v6 post-mortem where findings became per-case pins shaped like their triggering incidents, none falsified and none removable. Doctrine prose only — no script, no schema, no host contract change.
